scope: Minimal exceptional 27^3 route, its Spin(10) vector mediator, the established gauge-dressed Z9 lift, and the seven-versus-nine component mask.

claims.title: A primitive rank-one exceptional vacuum cannot select a non-scalar subspace of the Spin(10) vector
claims.statement: The Spin(10)-equivariant commutant on the irreducible 10 is scalar, so the first rank-one vacuum cannot distinguish the seven retained component vertices from the two diquark vertices.
dependencies: primitive rank-one vacuum with Spin(10) stabilizer
one irreducible Spin(10) vector mediator
falsifiers: an explicit non-scalar Spin(10)-equivariant idempotent on the irreducible vector 10

claims.title: The established Z9 lift is neutral on all nine 16-16-10 component vertices
claims.statement: The four ordinary Yukawa, three retained Furey/leptoquark, and two excluded diquark component vertices all have total charge zero modulo nine.
dependencies: neutral electroweak Higgs
the nine-component decomposition catalogued in document 1073
falsifiers: a corrected field orientation showing nonzero total Z9 charge for DQQ or D-dagger u^c d^c
a different derived Z9 lift that preserves all seven target vertices while charging both excluded vertices

claims.title: Z9 cannot enforce the exact seven-versus-nine vertex mask
claims.statement: Because both excluded diquark vertices are Z9-neutral, their absence cannot follow from this symmetry. Deleting them requires an independent incidence, boundary, Clebsch, or limiting-mass datum.
dependencies: EXCEPTIONAL-Z9-NINE-VERTEX-NEUTRALITY
falsifiers: a Z9-covariant representation-theoretic rule, not an added zero, that removes exactly the two neutral diquark intertwiners

claims.title: Z9 forbids leptoquark-diquark mixing while retaining both diagonal source sectors
claims.statement: TD and T-dagger D have nonzero charge, whereas T-dagger T and D-dagger D are neutral. If the lift is exact in the complete finite theory, the heavy Schur complement is block diagonal and the proton-decay cross exchange is absent.
dependencies: the Z9 lift is admitted by the complete finite normalizer
the three-family discrete anomaly conditions remain satisfied after all heavy fermions are included
the vacuum does not break the faithful baryon-triality quotient
falsifiers: an allowed heavy spurion with a nonzero vacuum expectation value that neutralizes TD or T-dagger D
a finite-Dirac block or anomaly that excludes the Z9 lift
a threshold diagram generating T-D cross propagation without breaking Z9

claims.title: No single singlet charge preserves both components of the minimal exceptional 1-10-10 threshold
claims.statement: In the minimal 27^3 cubic, x H_u H_d requires q_x=0 mod 9 while x T D requires q_x=3 mod 9. Thus no single Z9 eigencharge for the Spin(10) singlet x preserves the complete 1-10-10 invariant.
dependencies: one Spin(10)-singlet x with a definite Z9 charge
q(H_uH_d)=0 and q(TD)=6 mod 9
falsifiers: a component decomposition of the same minimal invariant in which H_uH_d and TD do not share x
a single q_x satisfying both modular invariance equations
a derived modification of the field charges consistent with all seven target vertices and anomaly constraints that equalizes the two bilinear charges

claims.title: A heavy diquark companion can only give an approximate seven-channel low-energy mask without another selector
claims.statement: Hermitian masses are Z9-allowed and may place D above the working scale, but Z9 neither forces the hierarchy nor deletes the D vertices. A quantitative conclusion requires a derived scalar potential and threshold spectrum.
dependencies: a nonsupersymmetric or otherwise Hermitian heavy-mass sector
a dynamically selected hierarchy m_D much greater than the observation scale
exact T-D block protection
falsifiers: a scalar potential theorem forcing a unique protected hierarchy and exact decoupling
threshold corrections that erase the hierarchy or regenerate cross mixing

claims.title: A 10 plus anti-126 Clebsch combination can algebraically realize the five coloured source conditions
claims.statement: On the aligned family-texture locus F proportional to H, the triplet weights (-2,1,1) on (10, anti-126 SU5 5, anti-126 SU5 50) kill QQ while retaining equal-and-opposite u^c e^c and d^c nu^c. The antitriplet weights (1,-1) on (10, anti-126 SU5 anti-45) kill u^c d^c while retaining QL.
dependencies: the component Clebsches in arXiv:2203.07748 with representation-wide normalizations absorbed into mixing coefficients
the Spin(10) right-pair orientation certified in document 1073
F proportional to H
the selected scalar mass eigenvectors equal the displayed kernel vectors
falsifiers: a corrected normalized Clebsch table making either displayed kernel inconsistent
proof that the required Standard-Model triplet components cannot mix after Spin(10) breaking

claims.title: Generic three-family 10 and anti-126 Yukawa tensors do not admit the Clebsch cancellation
claims.statement: The two diquark matrix cancellations require nonzero scalar coefficients satisfying aH+bF=0. For generic independent symmetric H and F this has only the trivial solution; a nonzero selector requires F proportional to H.
dependencies: H and F are independent symmetric family tensors
scalar mixing coefficients are family-blind numbers
falsifiers: a nontrivial solution for linearly independent H and F without adding family-dependent mediator mixing
a derived flavor symmetry that forces F proportional to H and fixes the remaining relative coefficient

claims.title: The 120 cannot cancel the symmetric-family diquark maps or supply same-family Furey links
claims.statement: The 120 Yukawa tensor G is antisymmetric while the 10 and anti-126 tensors H and F are symmetric. Symmetric and antisymmetric projections of a cancellation equation vanish separately, and G_AA is identically zero.
dependencies: 16 tensor 16 equals (10 plus 126)_symmetric plus 120_antisymmetric
the target mask is required as a full family-matrix identity
falsifiers: a same-generation 120 Yukawa entry consistent with G transpose equals minus G
a nonzero matrix simultaneously symmetric and antisymmetric over characteristic zero

claims.title: The distinct-Clebsch cancellation is not protected by Spin(10) representation content alone
claims.statement: The 10, 120 and 126 are inequivalent irreducible representations, so a symmetry commuting with Spin(10) cannot exchange them or fix the required nonzero ratios. Allowed perturbations of Yukawa alignment and the broken-phase mass matrix regenerate the diquark maps.
dependencies: no additional enlarged symmetry or finite-geometry selector
generic counterterms allowed by the broken-phase symmetry
canonical positive kinetic metric
falsifiers: an explicit anomaly-consistent symmetry that derives both Yukawa alignment and the two mediator kernel vectors
a nonrenormalization theorem preserving the cancellation locus in the full heavy theory

claims.title: The antitriplet Clebsch pair admits a safe-danger exchange parity after Spin(10) breaking
claims.statement: In the (10, anti-126 anti-45) component basis, u^c d^c=(1,1) is exchange-even and QL=(-1,1) is exchange-odd. A component Z2 can protect their separation, but it cannot extend as an exchange of the complete inequivalent Spin(10) multiplets.
dependencies: equal canonical component normalizations after rescaling
a broken-phase mass and kinetic operator invariant under the component exchange
falsifiers: a corrected Clebsch sign making the two source covectors nonorthogonal
an unavoidable threshold term that breaks the component exchange

claims.title: No unitary finite symmetry separates the complete triplet danger source from both retained sources in the canonical metric
claims.statement: The canonical Gram products are <QQ,u^c e^c>=2 and <QQ,d^c nu^c>=-2. Inequivalent unitary symmetry sectors must be orthogonal, so QQ cannot carry a different protecting character while the complete retained Clebsch covectors remain present.
dependencies: the three-column Clebsch basis of exceptional frontier 03
canonical positive mediator kinetic metric
the protecting symmetry acts unitarily
falsifiers: a corrected Clebsch basis with both danger-safe Gram products zero
a derived physical positive metric, compatible with the full finite theory, in which the sectors are orthogonal

claims.title: An irreducible real family-triplet algebra enforces Yukawa texture proportionality but not its coefficient
claims.statement: The commutant of the defining SO(3)_F action is one-dimensional, so invariant symmetric tensors have H=hI and F=fI. This gives F proportional to H when nonzero, but leaves f/h and all mediator mixing vectors free.
dependencies: three families in the defining irreducible real SO(3)_F representation
the family symmetry is exact at the selector scale
falsifiers: a nonscalar matrix commuting with all three defining SO(3) generators
a derivation of the mediator kernel vectors from the family action alone

claims.title: The minimal algebraic incidence selector is oblique and fails canonical adjoint closure
claims.statement: The projector onto ker(QQ) along ker(u^c e^c) intersect ker(d^c nu^c) is idempotent but not self-adjoint in the canonical metric. It kills QQ in one orientation, while its adjoint gives the nonzero source vector (1,-1/2,-1/2).
dependencies: canonical Hilbert metric
physical reality/self-adjoint closure includes the adjoint orientation
falsifiers: a represented junk relation that removes the adjoint-restored danger without deleting a retained source
a derived noncanonical physical metric making the same idempotent self-adjoint

claims.title: An adapted positive metric can make the safe-danger incidence projector self-adjoint
claims.statement: For the algebraic direct-sum basis B, G=(B^{-1})^dagger B^{-1} is positive and satisfies GP=P^dagger G. This supplies a mathematically consistent protected-sector template, but G and the corresponding central idempotent are not derived from the current finite spectral data.
dependencies: a broken-phase finite Hilbert metric allowed to mix the 10 and anti-126 component sectors
a represented C_safe plus C_danger central algebra
compatibility with D_F, J_F, grading, first order, junk, and all heavy thresholds
falsifiers: proof that every admissible physical metric is block diagonal between the relevant representation components
failure of reality, first-order, or junk closure for every explicit finite representation
a symmetry-allowed heavy threshold connecting the two central sectors

claims.title: The adapted safe-danger projection admits a consistent KO-six finite carrier
claims.statement: On H_F=V_+ plus V_-, the adapted-metric representation of C_safe plus C_danger, swap-conjugation J, odd grading, and block Dirac operator M=m_s P+m_d Q satisfy the star representation, KO-six signs, order zero, first order, and exact threshold block closure.
dependencies: the adapted positive metric G from wave-2 exceptional 01
P and Q are supplied as the central representation projectors
the finite Dirac and all heavy Hessians commute with P
falsifiers: a failed exact matrix identity in the finite-triple certificate
a symmetry-respecting threshold whose inverse does not commute with P

claims.title: The minimal safe-danger centre is protected only when its represented differential is trivial
claims.statement: If [D_F,P]=0, the central split survives fluctuations and thresholds but Omega^1_D(C plus C)=0. If [D_F,P] is nonzero, the represented cross one-forms have rank two, survive degree-one junk, and generate the forbidden mixing; in the minimal symmetric real representation first order also fails.
dependencies: faithful multiplicity-(2,1) representation of C plus C
minimal symmetric KO-six doubling
the cross Dirac support tested in the certificate
falsifiers: a nonzero represented central-label one-form that is junk while a nontrivial safe within-sector calculus survives
a cross-sector Dirac edge that preserves the central superselection character
an error in the degree-one universal-calculus rank computation

claims.title: C plus C with multiplicities two plus one does not derive the Clebsch-aligned projector
claims.statement: The admissible rank-two projector embeddings form Gr_C(2,3)=CP^2. The abstract algebra, KO signs, grading and first-order condition determine ranks but not the point ker(QQ); inserting P into the representation or D_F is an additional superselection orientation datum.
dependencies: three-dimensional complex mediator multiplicity space
safe and danger central multiplicities two and one
no larger algebra or derived operator selecting a unique projector
falsifiers: an invariant construction from already established Jordan, Furey, or exceptional data that uniquely selects ker(QQ)
a larger finite algebra whose representation has the desired P as its unique central spectral projector without inserting it

claims.title: A nontrivial base finite geometry can be tensored with the trivial-differential selector factor
claims.statement: A_F=B_F tensor (C_safe plus C_danger) can generate gauge and Higgs one-forms through B_F within each central block while the selector factor remains superselected. This is coherent only if J, grading, D_F, junk, and every heavy threshold preserve the central blocks.
dependencies: an explicit nontrivial base finite triple B_F
block-diagonal tensor-product Dirac support
all physical source maps assigned consistently to one central character
falsifiers: a required base one-form crossing the safe-danger centre
a reality or first-order condition identifying the two central characters
a heavy threshold carrying both characters

claims.title: Both two-ray source currents have nonzero complete local U(1) anomaly data
claims.statement: For one SM-plus-nu_R generation in the all-left basis and y6=6Y, the deduplicated ray has anomaly tuple (SU3^2X,SU2^2X,Y^2X,YX^2,grav^2X,X^3)=(16,16,336,-144,51,1131), while the multiplicity ray has (16,16,408,-96,53,1157). Neither is an exact ungarnished gauge symmetry.
dependencies: the wave-2 rays lambda_d=(5,5,1,1,1,0,0) and lambda_m=(5,5,1,1,3,0,0)
one-generation SM-plus-nu_R chiral multiplicities
integer hypercharge normalization y6=6Y
falsifiers: a corrected field orientation or multiplicity changing the exact trace calculation
a nonzero scalar contribution incorrectly omitted from a chiral fermion anomaly

claims.title: The minimal Green-Schwarz EFT completes both source rays and selects neither
claims.statement: A shifting Stueckelberg pseudoscalar with independent Wess-Zumino coefficients can cancel the local anomaly polynomial of either ray. With only one shifting phase it is eaten by the gauged U(1); retaining a physical ALP requires a second phase and introduces a new mixing direction.
dependencies: four-dimensional Green-Schwarz/Wess-Zumino anomaly cancellation
independent coefficients for the allowed gauge-topological operators
one connected gauged U(1)_X
falsifiers: a consistency relation forcing the required Wess-Zumino coefficient vector for exactly one ray
a one-phase Higgs or Stueckelberg realization leaving an additional uneaten physical pseudoscalar

claims.title: Anomaly cancellation cannot see the CP2 embedding of the safe projector
claims.statement: For X_V=x_s P+x_d(1-P), all character traces are 2x_s^n+x_d^n and are invariant under P to UPU-dagger. Chiral anomaly equations therefore depend on eigenvalues and multiplicities but are constant on Gr_C(2,3)=CP2, so they cannot correlate either ALP ray with the Clebsch-aligned projector.
dependencies: rank-two safe and rank-one danger character multiplicities
no independently supplied source-to-mediator intertwiner
standard anomaly traces over chiral fermion representations
falsifiers: a local or global anomaly invariant depending on mediator eigenvectors rather than representation characters
an already-derived cross-module operator making the relative orientation part of the gauge representation

claims.title: One source spurion either leaves the projector unprotected or protects an inserted orientation
claims.statement: If all broken-phase mediators have one character, the neutral operator |Phi|^2 v-dagger A v admits generic Hermitian A and misaligns P through thresholds. Distinct safe and danger characters force A to commute with P, but defining those characters as x_s P+x_d(1-P) has already supplied P.
dependencies: all gauge-invariant quadratic counterterms are admitted
one complex source order parameter
the three mediators have identical broken-phase Standard-Model quantum numbers
falsifiers: a symmetry not containing P that forbids every misaligning Hermitian counterterm
a dynamical vacuum theorem uniquely selecting the Clebsch plane from orientation-free couplings

claims.title: A larger two-plus-one finite algebra still leaves the relative Clebsch embedding free
claims.statement: M2(C) plus C canonically distinguishes abstract block dimensions, but conjugate representations sweep out the same CP2 family relative to the external Clebsch covectors. A finite Dirac map T can select P as a kernel or spectral projector only by carrying the missing source-to-mediator orientation itself.
dependencies: the Clebsch covectors define an external frame on the mediator multiplicity space
unitarily equivalent abstract finite-algebra representations are not distinguished without a cross-module map
no independently derived T is presently available
falsifiers: a unique representation embedding forced by the complete real spectral-triple axioms and existing data
an independently derived Jordan/Furey operator whose kernel is exactly the safe Clebsch plane and whose counterterms preserve it

claims.title: Existing Furey operators leave a full U(3) commutant on the exceptional triplet multiplicity
claims.statement: On the minimal common carrier, the established gauge action, grading, TRO/linking operators, electron face, and Dirac/Yukawa support act as Furey-side operators tensor the identity on the three-dimensional exceptional mediator multiplicity. Their joint commutant therefore contains U(3), which acts transitively on Gr_C(2,3)=CP2 and selects no rank-two projector.
dependencies: the presently established Furey data act on the matter-arrow carrier
the three broken-phase triplet copies have one Standard-Model gauge type
no non-scalar Furey-to-mediator intertwiner has been supplied
falsifiers: an already-derived Furey operator with a documented non-scalar action on the triplet multiplicity space
an explicit cross-carrier representation whose joint commutant has finite orbit on CP2
a calculation showing that the existing electron or Yukawa support canonically normalizes a mediator-copy covector

claims.title: KO-six reality leaves CP2, and even internal fixed reality leaves RP2
claims.statement: The particle-antiparticle swap-conjugation represents a multiplicity projector as P plus conjugate(P), so every Hermitian P is reality compatible and CP2 remains. Imposing the stronger extra condition P=conjugate(P) reduces the family only to Gr_R(2,3)=RP2, on which O(3) is transitive with a two-dimensional orbit.
dependencies: KO-six swap-conjugation real structure
rank-two Hermitian multiplicity projector
falsifiers: a KO-six identity that forces P to a finite set rather than pairing it with conjugate(P)
a failure of the O(3) tangent orbit on real rank-two projectors to have dimension two

claims.title: One transported safe electron line leaves a continuous projector family
claims.statement: Even if the Furey electron line is granted a nonzero image a in the exceptional multiplicity space and required to lie in the safe plane, the danger line remains arbitrary in a-perpendicular. The residual family is CP1, or RP1 under the stronger fixed-real condition; the complete generic stabilizer invariant is the principal angle Tr(A_e P).
dependencies: a transported electron line in mediator multiplicity space
the electron line is physically safe rather than the QQ danger line
falsifiers: a unique rank-two plane containing one fixed complex line without additional structure
an independently derived second anchor or phase/orientation datum already present in the corpus

claims.title: The QQ covector uniquely selects its kernel projector once imported
claims.statement: For A_QQ=q_QQ dagger q_QQ divided by its norm, the nonnegative functional F_QQ(P)=Tr(A_QQ P) on rank-two Hermitian projectors vanishes uniquely at P=I-A_QQ, whose image is ker(q_QQ). This proves uniqueness after the exceptional Clebsch covector is supplied, but the current Furey geometry does not derive that covector or its normalization on the mediator multiplicity.
dependencies: q_QQ=(1,1,1) in the declared exceptional Clebsch normalization
the canonical positive metric on the multiplicity space
falsifiers: a second rank-two Hermitian projector with zero F_QQ
an existing derivation of q_QQ as a normalized Furey-to-mediator covector
failure of the displayed projector to annihilate q_QQ dagger

claims.title: The grading-compatible Hom from Furey fermionic matter to the bosonic mediator is zero
claims.statement: Although the selected d-conjugate matter block shares the internal Standard-Model representation of an S1 scalar and gauge covariance alone would allow a C3 multiplicity Hom, the matter block is fermionic odd and the scalar mediator is bosonic even. The even intertwiner equation gives Y=-Y, so the gauge-, grading-compatible direct matter-to-mediator Hom is zero.
dependencies: the physical fermion/boson Z2 grading
the mediator is a bosonic scalar
intertwiners are required to preserve grading
falsifiers: a nonzero even map satisfying gamma_W Y=Y gamma_M between opposite grading signs
a declared odd mediator or parity-changing physical intertwiner with a complete Lorentz/statistics interpretation

claims.title: The bosonic Furey S1 embedding is normalized by the TRO but remains CP2-valued
claims.statement: For one bosonic Furey S1 source and three identical S1 mediator copies, gauge and grading compatible maps form C3. Requiring a nonzero map to preserve the ternary product forces norm(y)=1; conjugate-pair reality maps y to conjugate(y) and imposes no further restriction. Modulo the source phase, normalized embeddings form CP2.
dependencies: the optional colored Furey S1 fluctuation branch
three target copies of the same irreducible Standard-Model scalar representation
column-TRO composition on the copy multiplicities
falsifiers: a different dimension for Hom_G(S1,S1 tensor C3)
a unit-norm TRO morphism condition that selects a unique projective line
a KO reality equation reducing y beyond conjugate pairing

claims.title: Naturality under the existing mediator commutant forbids a canonical non-scalar Furey Gram
claims.statement: The surviving U3 copy automorphism has no nonzero fixed vector in C3, while its invariant Hermitian endomorphisms are exactly the real scalar multiples of I3. A chosen bosonic map produces a rank-one non-scalar y y-dagger, but its CP2 image line is free; a construction natural under all established automorphisms yields either the zero linear map or kappa I3.
dependencies: no already-derived non-scalar action on the mediator-copy labels
the current Furey incidence acts on source endpoints rather than unified scalar origins
canonical means natural under automorphisms of all declared input data
falsifiers: a nonzero U3-fixed vector in the defining representation
a non-scalar Hermitian matrix commuting with all of U3
an independently derived Furey-to-copy representation reducing the commutant before the map is chosen
